label: Calculating with Points on Lines
notes: Open by stating the chapter goal plainly: we want arithmetic on a projective line without smuggling in a metric ruler. Stress that every construction uses only joins and meets of points and lines, yet the endpoints will behave exactly like real numbers obeying the field axioms.

label: The Working Line and Homogeneous Pairs
notes: Explain that a point of the projective line is a homogeneous pair, defined up to nonzero scaling. The cross-ratio is the only projective invariant of four collinear points, and its determinant formula is the engine behind every later identity. Emphasize scale-invariance and the role of infinity.

label: Harmonic Quadruples: The Fourth Point Is Forced
notes: Define a harmonic quadruple by cross-ratio minus one. The key teaching point is rigidity: fix three points and the fourth harmonic partner is uniquely determined, independent of the auxiliary web used to build it. Connect minus one to its invariance under swapping either pair.

label: The Complete Quadrilateral Construction
notes: Walk through the complete quadrilateral as the pure-incidence machine that produces the harmonic conjugate. Trace the diagonal points and emphasize that only joins and meets appear. Two different auxiliary points yield the same fourth point, which is the visual proof of construction independence on the line.

label: Projective Scales: Choosing 0, 1 and Infinity
notes: Introduce the projective scale as the act of naming three anchors zero, one, and infinity. The coordinate of any other point is recovered as a cross-ratio against those anchors. Stress that visible spacing may distort under reparametrization, but the anchor-based coordinate is invariant.

label: Harmonic Conjugate as the +1 Step
notes: Show that repeatedly taking harmonic conjugates against fixed anchors steps the coordinate by one, generating the integer points. This is the geometric plus-one. Doubling and midpoints follow from specific harmonic identities, so the integer lattice on the line is purely synthetic.

label: Von Staudt Addition
notes: Present von Staudt addition through the affine chart where infinity is the horizontal direction, so lines toward infinity are parallel horizontals. Build the auxiliary points P and Q off the line, project x and y, and read the meeting point on the base line as x plus y. Highlight symmetry in x and y.

label: Von Staudt Multiplication
notes: Explain multiplication using the unit point one as the pivot. The construction projects through P and Q with the one anchor controlling the scaling ray, returning the product on the base line. Contrast with addition: here the unit, not infinity, plays the special structural role that fixes the multiplicative identity.

label: The Field Axioms, Realized Geometrically
notes: Summarize that the two constructions satisfy associativity, commutativity, distributivity, identities, and inverses. Each axiom corresponds to a closing incidence diagram. The slide frames the punchline: the points of a line, with geometric plus and times, form a field isomorphic to the coordinate field.

label: Pappos and the Commutativity of Multiplication
notes: Make the deep link explicit: the two recipes for x times y and y times x overlay into the Pappos configuration. Over the reals they coincide automatically, but synthetically Pappos's theorem is the incidence axiom that forces commutative multiplication. This is where geometry dictates algebra.

label: The Fundamental Theorem: Synthetic Meets Analytic
notes: State the bridge theorem. Coordinates recovered from pure incidence agree with analytic coordinates up to projective transformation, and a harmonic map fixing the anchors is forced to be a field automorphism. Over the ordered reals this leaves only the identity, tying synthetic and analytic projective geometry together.

label: Recap and Takeaways
notes: Recap the arc: harmonic quadruples give the first line invariant, a scale turns three anchors into coordinates, von Staudt addition and multiplication realize the field operations, and Pappos guarantees commutativity. Send students off with the message that incidence alone is enough to build arithmetic.
